# ABHEDYA System Architecture Document
Version: 1.1 · corrected architecture traceability, derived from the ABHEDYA v2 project pack.
Project: TM005136 · SFIC 2026 · PS0001 · secure, isolated, auditable cybersecurity testing platform.
Authority: `docs/02_MASTER_PLAN.md`, `docs/03_CONTEXT.md`, `docs/04_CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/06_VERIFICATION.md`, and `contracts/`.
This document describes architecture intent; it is not evidence that code has been implemented or verified.
Frozen machine-readable contracts are authoritative; a discrepancy requires an agreed change request.
Deployment is one Ubuntu Server 24.04 VM on the HP Omen demo host, with an imported VM on the Legion as backup.
The demo host is prepared for offline use; images, dependency wheels, rules, probe sets, TLS and secrets are preloaded.
The browser enters through proxy TLS 443; no API, database, runner, or notary port is published to the LAN.
The proxy serves the React console and forwards `/api/v1` on the internal control network.
The API authenticates, authorizes, validates, and writes desired state; it has no Docker Engine connection.
PostgreSQL is the coordination point: API and runner communicate through rows, while NOTIFY carries event identifiers.
The runner reconciles desired environment/job rows into Docker objects and is the sole holder of the Docker socket.
The notary reads the audit prefix, signs Merkle roots with Ed25519, and writes a witness copy outside PostgreSQL.
The standalone verifier checks exported audit material without importing `core/` or `services/`.
Each environment owns an internal isolated bridge, labels, quota volume, and separately limited containers.
Every container uses the profile in `docs/04_CONTRACTS.md` section 8; normal runtime is gVisor `runsc`.
Degraded `runc-hardened` mode is available only when explicitly configured and must raise visible isolation-degraded status.
Admin and auditor roles cannot execute commands in tenant environments or read job outputs under R17–R21.
The prototype is single-host; it does not claim high availability, hardware side-channel defense, or independent external witnessing.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · edge ingress: Only proxy TLS 443 is published; request URI is the contracted `/api/v1` path and proxy never performs RBAC.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · transport and service reachability: Request goes browser -> proxy -> API on `control`; API has no published port and no Docker socket.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · identity/session: Login verifies Argon2id and lockout; successful login creates the opaque session and returns the caller CSRF token.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · CSRF gate: This route is read-only or public login; it has no state-changing CSRF check to bypass.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · RBAC rule: R01 is explicitly `public: true`; login validates credentials before assigning a role or creating a session.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · object scope: No object lookup occurs for anonymous request; authorization response precedes row data.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · request schema: Validate exact JSON/multipart shape and bounds before opening a state-changing transaction.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · database role and row access: Use `abh_api` and parameterized SQL next to handler; never connect as schema owner at runtime.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · state ownership and transaction: GET performs a scoped read; POST/PATCH/DELETE mutation, desired-state change, and its audit append share one short transaction where specified.
Route architecture · R01 `POST /auth/login` · actor=anonymous (no role asserted) · case=valid credentials · audit semantics: On successful mutation append exactly one `auth.login` success record through `abh_core.audit.append` in the mutation transaction.

Component interface C-PROXY-01: proxy — Publishes TLS 443 on demo interface.
Component interface C-PROXY-02: proxy — Serves the built React console as static content.
Component interface C-PROXY-03: proxy — Forwards `/api/v1` to API over control network.
Component interface C-PROXY-04: proxy — Does not authenticate roles or make database authorization decisions.
Component interface C-PROXY-05: proxy — Has no PostgreSQL role.
Component interface C-PROXY-06: proxy — Has no Docker socket mount.
Component interface C-PROXY-07: proxy — Carries request ID through to API response.
Component interface C-PROXY-08: proxy — Disables SSE buffering and compression on `/stream`.
Component interface C-API-01: API — Runs FastAPI under the unprivileged service container.
Component interface C-API-02: API — Uses `abh_api` database login.
Component interface C-API-03: API — Loads `rbac_matrix.yaml` as the authorization source.
Component interface C-API-04: API — Fails app startup if a registered route is missing from the matrix.
Component interface C-API-05: API — Writes desired state but not observed runner state.
Component interface C-API-06: API — Never opens Docker API/socket.
Component interface C-API-07: API — Uses parameterized SQL adjacent to handler code.
Component interface C-API-08: API — Appends audit through `abh_core.audit.append` only.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-01: PostgreSQL — Stores tenancy, identity, sessions, envs, jobs, metrics, activity, audit and checkpoints.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-02: PostgreSQL — Applies `contracts/schema.sql` once with owner role at initialization.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-03: PostgreSQL — Runtime services use `abh_api`, `abh_runner`, or `abh_notary`.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-04: PostgreSQL — Audit log triggers reject UPDATE, DELETE, and TRUNCATE for normal access.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-05: PostgreSQL — NOTIFY payloads carry activity row IDs and audit sequence numbers.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-06: PostgreSQL — Database does not expose a host-published port.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-07: PostgreSQL — Only short control transactions occur; no Docker work holds a DB lock.
Component interface C-POSTGRESQL-08: PostgreSQL — Owner credentials are not used by runtime processes.
Component interface C-RUNNER-01: runner — Uses `abh_runner` database login.
Component interface C-RUNNER-02: runner — Is sole service with Docker socket mount.
Component interface C-RUNNER-03: runner — Polls/reconciles DB rows instead of accepting HTTP requests.
Component interface C-RUNNER-04: runner — Is sole writer of observed_state, isolation_tier, failure_reason.
Component interface C-RUNNER-05: runner — Performs container work before opening short result/state transaction.
Component interface C-RUNNER-06: runner — Uses one `launch` primitive for all workload containers.
Component interface C-RUNNER-07: runner — Applies labels for managed/env/team/template reconciliation.
Component interface C-RUNNER-08: runner — Emits activity, metrics and audit with its service actor.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-01: Docker Engine — Runs on Ubuntu demo VM and is inside trusted computing base.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-02: Docker Engine — Uses `runsc` runtime for sandbox containers by default.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-03: Docker Engine — Creates one internal bridge and volume namespace per environment.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-04: Docker Engine — Does not publish sandbox ports.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-05: Docker Engine — Uses labels as lookup keys but not as a substitute for DB authorization.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-06: Docker Engine — Runner daemon access is root-equivalent and restricted to the runner.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-07: Docker Engine — Runs preloaded digest-pinned images with pull policy never.
Component interface C-DOCKER-ENGINE-08: Docker Engine — Is never controlled directly by API request handlers.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-01: sandbox — Uses UID:GID 1000:1000.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-02: sandbox — Drops ALL Linux capabilities and adds none.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-03: sandbox — Enables no-new-privileges.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-04: sandbox — Uses a read-only root filesystem.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-05: sandbox — Mounts `/tmp` as 64 MiB rw,noexec,nosuid tmpfs.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-06: sandbox — Mounts only quota `/workspace` and template-defined data.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-07: sandbox — Does not receive host namespaces, devices, host directory, or Docker socket.
Component interface C-SANDBOX-08: sandbox — Does not receive ABH_ secrets, database credentials, or notary key.
Component interface C-NOTARY-01: notary — Uses `abh_notary` database login.
Component interface C-NOTARY-02: notary — Reads audit sequence and checkpoints; appends checkpoint records.
Component interface C-NOTARY-03: notary — Signs Ed25519 checkpoint body with a 32-byte secret seed.
Component interface C-NOTARY-04: notary — Uses cadence of 20 records or 30 seconds.
Component interface C-NOTARY-05: notary — Writes signed checkpoint copy to witness NDJSON outside DB volume.
Component interface C-NOTARY-06: notary — Stops further trusted signing if existing history fails verification.
Component interface C-NOTARY-07: notary — Emits audit/activity tamper signal when a mismatch is confirmed.
Component interface C-NOTARY-08: notary — Does not run workloads or receive Docker socket.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-01: witness file — Lives outside PostgreSQL data volume.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-02: witness file — Contains signed checkpoint records, not private signing material.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-03: witness file — Is mounted writable only into notary for appends.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-04: witness file — Is an input to standalone verification and evidence packaging.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-05: witness file — Protects against DB-only rewrite when a prior copy is retained.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-06: witness file — Shares same-host operator risk and is not an independent witness.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-07: witness file — Must be included in offline demo evidence.
Component interface C-WITNESS-FILE-08: witness file — Write failure is visible and cannot be called durable external anchoring.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-01: verifier — Is `tools/verify_audit.py` runnable on another machine.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-02: verifier — Imports nothing from `core/` or `services/`.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-03: verifier — Reads newline-delimited export, public key, optional witness.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-04: verifier — Recomputes canonical record bytes and SHA-256 chain.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-05: verifier — Recomputes RFC 6962 Merkle roots and checkpoint signatures.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-06: verifier — Returns exit 0 for valid input, 2 for detected tamper, 3 for usage/input error.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-07: verifier — Reports first failure verdict and sequence/tree position.
Component interface C-VERIFIER-08: verifier — Never needs a live DB connection or private key.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-01: console — Is a React static bundle served by proxy.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-02: console — Shows environment desired and observed states separately.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-03: console — Shows `gvisor` or explicit degraded `runc-hardened` tier.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-04: console — Scopes lists and event views to the authenticated user's role/team.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-05: console — Shows live activity, resource graphs and critical alerts.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-06: console — Does not render user-supplied command/output as HTML.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-07: console — Labels scanner findings as scanner-flagged, not verified ground truth.
Component interface C-CONSOLE-08: console — Labels file `clean` as a triage result, not safe.
Component interface C-HOST-01: host — Is Ubuntu Server 24.04 inside the Omen virtualization host.
Component interface C-HOST-02: host — Runs host preflight before stack startup.
Component interface C-HOST-03: host — Confirms runsc, network isolation, storage enforcement, images and versions.
Component interface C-HOST-04: host — Keeps project files and secrets in documented paths.
Component interface C-HOST-05: host — Reserves host CPU/memory before admission.
Component interface C-HOST-06: host — Is the only current Docker daemon in use for demo.
Component interface C-HOST-07: host — Parth operates the single stack to avoid multiple reapers.
Component interface C-HOST-08: host — Henil's imported backup VM is preflighted and rehearsed before use.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-01: quarantine — Stores upload bytes by SHA-256 digest, never original filename path.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-02: quarantine — Enforces 10 MiB maximum before job admission.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-03: quarantine — Stores sample with mode 0400.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-04: quarantine — Is writable by API service and read-only to runner mount.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-05: quarantine — Is not mounted into general app-target or AI containers.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-06: quarantine — Feeds the analyzer and optional single-file read-only sample mount.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-07: quarantine — Is cleaned according to job/environment lifecycle.
Component interface C-QUARANTINE-08: quarantine — Is not claimed encrypted at rest.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-01: SSE service — Uses Server-Sent Events on R22.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-02: SSE service — Sends activity, audit, metric, and heartbeat event types.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-03: SSE service — Heartbeats are emitted every 15 seconds.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-04: SSE service — Activity event IDs are row IDs and support Last-Event-ID.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-05: SSE service — Filters event team scope on the server.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-06: SSE service — Does not send audit events to analysts.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-07: SSE service — Sends NOTIFY identifiers, then retrieves scoped row content.
Component interface C-SSE-SERVICE-08: SSE service — Targets state latency <=3 seconds and metric sample interval <=5 seconds.
Deployment service `proxy` attaches only to `edge + control`; this network placement is part of the trust model.
Deployment service `proxy` publishes `443 on demo interface`; no other listener is exposed to the host.
Deployment service `proxy` mounts `console build + TLS data`; mounts are the only declared host/container data boundary.
Deployment service `proxy` connects as `none`; no runtime service receives schema-owner credentials.
Deployment service `proxy` health/restart behavior is observed by stack operations; degraded status is not hidden.
Deployment service `api` attaches only to `control`; this network placement is part of the trust model.
Deployment service `api` publishes `none`; no other listener is exposed to the host.
Deployment service `api` mounts `quarantine rw`; mounts are the only declared host/container data boundary.
Deployment service `api` connects as `abh_api`; no runtime service receives schema-owner credentials.
Deployment service `api` health/restart behavior is observed by stack operations; degraded status is not hidden.
Deployment service `runner` attaches only to `control`; this network placement is part of the trust model.
Deployment service `runner` publishes `none`; no other listener is exposed to the host.
Deployment service `runner` mounts `Docker socket + quarantine ro + volume directory`; mounts are the only declared host/container data boundary.
Deployment service `runner` connects as `abh_runner`; no runtime service receives schema-owner credentials.
Deployment service `runner` health/restart behavior is observed by stack operations; degraded status is not hidden.
Deployment service `notary` attaches only to `control`; this network placement is part of the trust model.
Deployment service `notary` publishes `none`; no other listener is exposed to the host.
Deployment service `notary` mounts `notary key ro + witness rw`; mounts are the only declared host/container data boundary.
Deployment service `notary` connects as `abh_notary`; no runtime service receives schema-owner credentials.
Deployment service `notary` health/restart behavior is observed by stack operations; degraded status is not hidden.
Deployment service `db` attaches only to `control`; this network placement is part of the trust model.
Deployment service `db` publishes `none`; no other listener is exposed to the host.
Deployment service `db` mounts `database data`; mounts are the only declared host/container data boundary.
Deployment service `db` connects as `owner at init only`; no runtime service receives schema-owner credentials.
Deployment service `db` health/restart behavior is observed by stack operations; degraded status is not hidden.

Network edge `browser` -> `proxy` uses `HTTPS TLS 443` on `edge`; permitted payload is console and API requests.
Network edge `browser` -> `proxy` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `browser` -> `proxy` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `proxy` -> `api` uses `HTTP over internal control network` on `control`; permitted payload is forwarded /api/v1 request with request ID.
Network edge `proxy` -> `api` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `proxy` -> `api` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `api` -> `db` uses `PostgreSQL protocol on control` on `control`; permitted payload is authenticated API SQL under abh_api.
Network edge `api` -> `db` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `api` -> `db` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `runner` -> `db` uses `PostgreSQL protocol on control` on `control`; permitted payload is desired-state reads, observed-state/job/metric/activity/audit writes under abh_runner.
Network edge `runner` -> `db` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `runner` -> `db` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `notary` -> `db` uses `PostgreSQL protocol on control` on `control`; permitted payload is audit prefix/checkpoint read and checkpoint insert under abh_notary.
Network edge `notary` -> `db` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `notary` -> `db` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `runner` -> `Docker Engine` uses `Unix Docker socket` on `host-local runner mount`; permitted payload is create/inspect/stop/remove labeled sandbox objects.
Network edge `runner` -> `Docker Engine` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `runner` -> `Docker Engine` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `notary` -> `witness file` uses `local filesystem append` on `witness mount outside database volume`; permitted payload is signed checkpoint NDJSON.
Network edge `notary` -> `witness file` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `notary` -> `witness file` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `browser` -> `API` uses `no direct connection` on `not allowed`; permitted payload is browser always traverses proxy.
Network edge `browser` -> `API` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `browser` -> `API` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `control network` uses `no attachment/route` on `not allowed`; permitted payload is sandbox cannot reach API, DB, runner, or notary addresses.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `control network` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `control network` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `edge network` uses `no attachment/route` on `not allowed`; permitted payload is sandbox cannot use browser ingress or published proxy path.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `edge network` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `sandbox` -> `edge network` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `sandbox alpha` -> `sandbox bravo` uses `no shared network` on `not allowed`; permitted payload is per-environment network IDs prevent peer reachability.
Network edge `sandbox alpha` -> `sandbox bravo` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `sandbox alpha` -> `sandbox bravo` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.
Network edge `file detonator` -> `any network` uses `network none` on `not allowed`; permitted payload is detonation sample has loopback only and cannot reach a gateway.
Network edge `file detonator` -> `any network` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `file detonator` -> `any network` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.

Network edge `API` -> `Docker Engine` does not carry password hashes, raw session tokens, notary private seed, or unrelated team job output.
Network edge `API` -> `Docker Engine` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.

Network edge `notary` -> `Docker Engine` failure is visible at the owning service; there is no fallback to an unlisted route.

Risk register R-01 `Building on Windows with WSL or Docker Desktop`: architecture exposure is A gVisor maintainer calls WSL "very much unsupported" [S9]; Docker Desktop hides the daemon in its own VM.
Risk register R-01 mitigation path: Use a real Linux VM or machine from the first hour.
Risk register R-01 detection path: `preflight 1 to 4`; the architecture claim is limited to this observable proof.
Risk register R-01 recovery path: operator follows the recorded mitigation and does not silently select a weaker runtime or boundary.
Risk register R-01 residual: the project states the remaining limit in `docs/03_CONTEXT.md` or the risk entry; no untested assurance is added.

Audit architecture stage AU-01: Build exactly the 15-key body described in section 7.2 before computing the digest.
Audit architecture stage AU-02: Serialize canonical JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii=false, UTF-8 encoding.
Audit architecture stage AU-03: Reject floats and null before bytes are hashed.
Audit architecture stage AU-04: Format database UTC timestamps with six microsecond digits and literal Z.
Audit architecture stage AU-05: Acquire append serialization lock so concurrent writers cannot fork sequence order.
Audit architecture stage AU-06: Set seq to previous maximum plus one and prev_hash to the prior record digest.
Audit architecture stage AU-07: Compute record hash from canonical body with the contracted digest formula.
Audit architecture stage AU-08: Insert through `abh_core.audit.append`; no other application path inserts audit_log.
Audit architecture stage AU-09: For a successful state mutation, append occurs inside that mutation transaction.
Audit architecture stage AU-10: For a denied request, append one outcome=denied record as the RBAC contract requires; do not claim a state mutation exists.
Audit architecture stage AU-11: For anonymous 401 outside login, emit throttled activity rather than an audit row.
Audit architecture stage AU-12: After commit, NOTIFY carries the sequence number only.
Audit architecture stage AU-13: Notary reads a consistent prefix and computes Merkle root over ordered leaf hashes.
Audit architecture stage AU-14: Sign checkpoint body using Ed25519 seed read from protected secret file.
Audit architecture stage AU-15: Persist checkpoint and append witness record outside database storage.
Audit architecture stage AU-16: Verifier checks chain before checkpoint signatures and witness comparison in specified first-failure order.
Audit architecture stage AU-17: If verification fails, do not sign a new checkpoint over the suspect history.
Audit architecture stage AU-18: Raise tamper activity and UI alert within the 30-second objective window.
Schema architecture fact: `team` owns quota_envs, quota_cpu_millis, quota_mem_mb, quota_storage_mb and normalized tenant name.
Schema architecture fact: `app_user` binds role and team_id; admin/auditor are teamless, team_lead/analyst require team_id.
Schema architecture fact: `session` stores token_sha256, user_id, CSRF token, IP, user-agent and expiry; raw token is absent.
Schema architecture fact: `env` separates API desired_state from runner observed_state and stores isolation_tier/failure_reason.
Schema architecture fact: `job` binds kind, env_id, team_id, requester, input, status, result and lifecycle timestamps.
Schema architecture fact: `metric_sample` keys samples by env_id and timestamp and stores CPU, memory, storage, PIDs, RX and TX.
Schema architecture fact: `activity_event` carries optional team/env IDs, severity, kind, message and JSON data.
Schema architecture fact: `audit_log` stores version, sequence, canonical body fields, prev_hash and unique hash.
Schema architecture fact: `audit_checkpoint` stores tree size, root, head, timestamp, log ID, signature and creation time.
Schema architecture fact: `env_team_name_live` prevents a duplicate live name but permits reuse after destruction.
Schema architecture fact: `env_reconcile_idx` supports observed/desired-state reconciliation queries.
Schema architecture fact: `job_queue_idx` supports status/created_at queue scans; `job_team_idx` supports scoped history.
Schema architecture fact: `activity_team_idx` supports team-scoped descending event fetch.
Schema architecture fact: `audit_team_idx` and `audit_action_idx` support scoped and action-filtered audit reads.
Schema architecture fact: Audit immutability triggers guard UPDATE, DELETE, and TRUNCATE; cryptographic checks remain necessary against superuser.

R12 creation 01: authenticated team_lead or analyst supplies only name, `app-target`, size S/M/L and optional TTL; raw CPU/memory limits are not accepted.
R12 creation 02: API derives owner_id and team_id from the authenticated principal and never trusts a team_id supplied in JSON.
R12 creation 03: API validates environment name against the lower-case 3–32 character contract before allocation.
R12 creation 04: API maps S to 500 CPU millis, 256 MiB memory, 128 MiB storage, 128 PIDs.
R12 creation 05: API maps M to 1000 CPU millis, 512 MiB memory, 256 MiB storage, 256 PIDs.
R12 creation 06: API maps L to 2000 CPU millis, 1024 MiB memory, 512 MiB storage, 512 PIDs.
R12 creation 07: API locks the team quota row while comparing active allocation and the requested size.
R12 creation 08: API also checks aggregate host allocation after retaining configured CPU/memory reserve.
R12 creation 09: quota failure returns 409 QUOTA_EXCEEDED and writes a denied audit record; no env row is admitted.
R12 creation 10: successful insert starts with desired_state=running and observed_state=requested.
R12 creation 11: successful creation and `env.create` audit append share the API transaction.
R12 creation 12: runner observes the row after commit; API response does not claim a container is already running.
R12 creation 13: runner moves the row through provisioning and uses the single launch primitive.
R12 creation 14: runner creates the per-env network and volume before the managed containers.
R12 creation 15: runner sets labels that bind Docker objects to env_id, team_id and template.
R12 creation 16: runner inspects runtime/profile and records observed_state running only after checks succeed.
R12 creation 17: runner records isolation_tier=gvisor for the normal runtime; degraded mode is explicit.
R12 creation 18: provisioning failure records observed_state=failed and a bounded failure_reason for console visibility.
R12 creation 19: activity notification carries row ID; API fetches and scope-filters event details for the stream.
R12 creation 20: metrics begin only after observed_state is running; the runner samples at the configured interval.
R12 creation 21: default TTL is 60 minutes and the maximum TTL is 240 minutes.
R12 creation 22: environment name uniqueness applies while observed_state is not destroyed.
R12 creation 23: stop/destroy actions update desired state; runner later stops/removes runtime objects.
R12 creation 24: T-ISO, T-RES, T-AUD and T-E2E evidence inspect the runtime, quota, audit and visible lifecycle independently.
R30 kill switch 01: caller must be admin; auditor and all tenant roles fail the matrix check.
R30 kill switch 02: request carries team_id UUID or null; null means every team, as contracted.
R30 kill switch 03: API validates X-CSRF-Token before starting the mutation transaction.
R30 kill switch 04: API selects only environments matching requested team, or all live rows when team_id is null.
R30 kill switch 05: API changes desired_state to stopped and does not update observed_state directly.
R30 kill switch 06: API appends exactly one `admin.kill_switch` success record in the same transaction as desired-state changes.
R30 kill switch 07: response reports affected count; it does not claim all Docker containers stopped synchronously.
R30 kill switch 08: runner observes stopped desired state and performs Docker stop outside the API transaction.
R30 kill switch 09: runner commits observed_state and its service audit/activity after Docker work completes.
R30 kill switch 10: if Docker stop fails, env failure/state is visible and the runner retries according to reconciliation behavior.
R30 kill switch 11: SSE activity informs authorized viewers; admin overview reflects desired and observed state separately.
R30 kill switch 12: T-E2E-02 checks admin action and ledger evidence; RBAC tests deny non-admin callers.
R30 kill switch 13: repeated requests remain auditable and idempotent with respect to the stopped desired state.
R30 kill switch 14: a team-scoped kill switch leaves other teams' desired states unchanged.
R30 kill switch 15: global kill switch sets all targeted environments to stopped but does not erase audit history.
R30 kill switch 16: no route in the API turns this control into arbitrary command execution inside a sandbox.
R30 kill switch 17: no sandbox network path is used to deliver the kill signal; runner reads the DB state.
R30 kill switch 18: if PostgreSQL is unavailable, API cannot claim the kill request was accepted or audited.
R30 kill switch 19: if runner is down, desired state remains durable and is reconciled after runner restart.
R30 kill switch 20: evidence distinguishes accepted request time from actual Docker stop completion time.
R30 kill switch 21: platform confidentiality remains: stop capability does not grant admin job-output access.
R30 kill switch 22: event stream scope remains server-side even when the changed rows span many teams.
R30 kill switch 23: audit detail identifies whether team_id was supplied or null without storing secrets.
R30 kill switch 24: reviewer verifies targeted env rows, `admin.kill_switch` record, runner transition and console status.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · edge ingress: Only proxy TLS 443 is published; request URI is the contracted `/api/v1` path and proxy never performs RBAC.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · transport and service reachability: Request goes browser -> proxy -> API on `control`; API has no published port and no Docker socket.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · identity/session: Session token is opaque 32-byte CSPRNG material; DB stores only SHA-256, with 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute expiry.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · CSRF gate: This route is read-only or public login; it has no state-changing CSRF check to bypass.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · RBAC rule: Single authorization dependency resolves R18 in `contracts/rbac_matrix.yaml`; caller=authenticated `analyst`; configured scope=`own`.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · object scope: query binds `requested_by` to caller; peer-owned jobs are filtered from the list, never surfaced as 403/404.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · request schema: Contract defines no request body; there is no body-driven resource allocation at this route.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · database role and row access: Use `abh_api` and parameterized SQL next to handler; never connect as schema owner at runtime. Job output is tenant data; admin/auditor route denial prevents this read path.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · state ownership and transaction: GET performs a scoped read; POST/PATCH/DELETE mutation, desired-state change, and its audit append share one short transaction where specified.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · audit semantics: No success audit action is declared for this read; do not emit an invented mutation record.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · runner/Docker boundary: No direct Docker call from API; runner observes database rows and alone controls Docker socket.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · network path: API is reachable from proxy over internal control network; sandbox is not attached to this network.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · response status: 200; return only analyst-owned/requested jobs in the fixed list shape; omit peer rows without scope error.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · response data shape: Successful route shape is `contract-defined JSON resource/list shape; no additional fields`; never include password_hash, totp_secret, raw token, or unrelated team data.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · stream/activity visibility: Changes and alerts become activity/audit/metric events only through server-side scope filtering.
Route architecture · R18 `GET /jobs` · actor=authenticated `analyst` · case=list query under own scope · proof/test observation: Architecture proof is checked by route/object/scope cases in `docs/06_VERIFICATION.md`; route contract is - {id: R18, method: GET,    path: /jobs,                  allow: {team_lead: team, analyst: own}}.
R20 file flow 01: console sends multipart `file` plus `detonate` boolean; filename remains display metadata.
R20 file flow 02: proxy forwards the request to API over control; proxy does not write upload bytes to a host path.
R20 file flow 03: API enforces the 10 MiB bound before creating a job or runner work item.
R20 file flow 04: API computes SHA-256 from received bytes and uses the digest as quarantine object name.
R20 file flow 05: quarantine file mode is 0400; runner receives read-only access to the sample.
R20 file flow 06: original filename is never concatenated into a shell command or used as a host filesystem path.
R20 file flow 07: team_id and requested_by come from the authenticated analyst/team lead context, not upload fields.
R20 file flow 08: quota admission and file_analysis job insert happen before the runner claims the job.
R20 file flow 09: audit action `file.submit` records the accepted submission; failed admission records denied outcome.
R20 file flow 10: analyzer performs static type/hash/YARA triage before any optional execution stage.
R20 file flow 11: optional detonator starts only when detonate=true and uses Docker network none.
R20 file flow 12: detonator receives the single sample read-only, never the Docker socket or quarantine directory write access.
R20 file flow 13: detonation ends at the contracted 120-second cap; timeout contributes to suspicious verdict.
R20 file flow 14: verdict follows deterministic YARA/timeout/error rules; clean is not rendered as safe.
R20 file flow 15: file environment is size S with 10-minute TTL; container, network and volume are removed at completion/expiry.
R20 file flow 16: `T-WL-02` verifies malicious sample flag, benign sample result, network failure, digest path/mode, and cleanup.
R21 AI flow 01: request selects only `stub-vulnerable` or `stub-guarded`; arbitrary target URLs are not accepted.
R21 AI flow 02: request selects only the `quick` or `full` probe set defined by the local scanner image.
R21 AI flow 03: authenticated caller supplies no team override; team_id is bound from the principal.
R21 AI flow 04: quota admission precedes the ai_scan job insert; refusal does not launch scanner containers.
R21 AI flow 05: audit action `ai.scan_start` records the accepted scan; denial uses outcome=denied per RBAC contract.
R21 AI flow 06: AI environment uses size M and 10-minute TTL under the same runner launch primitive.
R21 AI flow 07: `llm-target` and `scanner` communicate inside only that environment's internal network.
R21 AI flow 08: target is an in-repo stub and probe resources are preloaded so the demo runs offline.
R21 AI flow 09: scanner cannot route to public internet or another environment during the mandatory offline test.
R21 AI flow 10: each probe result carries attempts, failures and an OWASP LLM risk identifier.
R21 AI flow 11: aggregate result carries attempts, failures, and report SHA-256 as defined by the Job shape.
